content: Master is failing to build, and the reason behind this is down to us not using a merge queue I believe. So I have enforced the use of the merge queue and fixed the master build here: Physlib#1713 (if someone could review this).
Another alternative to this would be this branch protection setting - "Require branches to be up to date before merging"
(both work, the above is just another suggestion :))
Ok, this is a good option to know about, as the merge queue might get annoying.

Ok, Merge queue fully set up; and seems to be working. One thing I had to do is turn off one of the branch protection rules. This in theory means that 'reviewers' as well as 'maintainers' can merge PRs. I think the solution to this is we just ask them not to.
Yes this is true, the merge sign is unblocked now.
Seems like an alright compromise, althought it's strange that the mergu queue does not work with this branch protection feature

Let M be the master branch at a given time. Let us say two pull requests A and B are made around the same time.

The linter for A checks M + A and the linter for B checks M + B.
If A merges the new master becomes M + A. Even if (M + A) + B fails, you could still merge B since M + B passed. This is what went wrong here.

The merge queue prevents this, and means that before B merges (M + A) + B must succeed.
(btw if people disagree with this very happy to discuss, just wanted to implement a fix now so we have things working + safe).
I see, so to each PR it looks okay but the combination fails. I think this seems reasonable
Yeah exactly. I think this only would ever happen if A was something like a bump or added a linter or something like that, but better safe then sorry.

I think something which will help with reviewing, is that whenever a PR is added to the merge queue the “ready-to-merge” label is added onto the PR if it is not already there. This will safe a step in merging PRs

Noob question: Is there no way to make adding to the merge queue automatic if the tag appears? Or given a command from one of the maintainers like add-merge-queueand then both the tag and the queue is done

For the second idea:
I think this would be possible via a GitHub workflow. It would have to check the permissions of the person commenting, but if that is possible then this should work.

i think this is a good solution, especially if the remark can also be written in an approval comment.

For the first: there are certain situations where we want to say “ready-to-merge” but do not want to actually merge it there and then.
I think a simple thing which would help here is if awaiting-author worked in review comments (both the individual comments or the overall one). It does not seem to.
